records.title: HCPA_Neighborhoods
records.description: The HCPA Neighborhoods layer represents generalized neighborhood areas within Hillsborough County, Florida, as defined for property assessment and market analysis purposes. Neighborhood boundaries are used to group properties with similar market characteristics, development patterns, or geographic influences. These boundaries are established for administrative and valuation analysis and may not correspond to officially recognized municipal neighborhoods, community boundaries, or homeowner association areas. This dataset is intended for mapping, reference, and analytical applications. Neighborhood boundaries are generalized for GIS display and are not intended for legal or survey purposes. Maintained by the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser.

records.title: CFIlocation20260106
records.description: CFI is used by government EM as a goal for the coordination of restoration and post disaster economic re‐development and in coordination with infrastructure service providers. This measure is intended to improve communication at county EOCs and other coordination centers during any type of emergency event. This alignment, as well as planning during peace time, ensures that community services are restored in a flexible and coordinated manner.Infrastructure service providers, such as electricity, gas, water, telecom, debris management, etc., use CFI as a guideline in the development and execution of their restoration processes and related priority rankings. It is understood that in the aftermath of an emergency event, it may take days or weeks to restore the critical infrastructure, depending on the severity of the event. The restoration approach is predicated on the type and geographical area of damage.Since “safety of life” is paramount during restoration and recovery, in the immediate aftermath of an event, restoration of the first four types of CFI 1 facilities will be most critical (hospitals, emergency shelters, main fire stations and water/wastewater facilities). These facilities will be given priority in sequence from top to bottom and all facilities are not equally weighted.
records.parentSummary: Authoritive point locations of Emergency Hospital (EMS) and Trauma Resources facilities maintained for organizational GIS use.

records.title: Study Area
records.description: ClearCast City of St. Petersburg coastal guidance. Observed window: previous 24 hours; forecast model horizon: 120 hours. STOFS2D daily baseline; valid local P-Surge enables e50 most-likely and e10 high-end coastal guidance with WPC P90 rainfall. Source cycle/advisory is recorded in latest-run metadata. Coastal inundation is derived by interpolating selected coastal forecast reference levels over terrain; rainfall is a separate guidance overlay, not a coupled rainfall/runoff simulation. Latest operational records replace previous records; event archives are maintained in Clearview Azure.
records.parentSummary: The SurgeCast_CoSP_AGOL layer contains key spatial datasets supporting coastal surge and rainfall forecasting for the City of St. Petersburg (CoSP). It integrates hydrometeorological inputs, modeled flood extents, and observed data to support visualization and decision-making within the SurgeCast platform.

records.title: CDBG_HUD_ProjectExtents_Polygons
records.description: CDBG Disaster Recovery Project - Polygons includes groupid sidewalk and road resurfacing projects for Community Development Block Grants for ACA HUD projects, includes 2020 LMISD data. HUD data from: Low to Moderate Income Population by Tract | HUD Open Data Site this is based on 2010 Census Tracts geography and the 2011-2015 ACS. Newer data is available at LMISD Map Application 2016-2020 - Overview and is based on the 2020 Census Blocks geography and the 2016-2020 ACS and is called Low Moderate Income Summary Data (LMISD) ACS 5-Year 2016-2020 Low- and Moderate-Income Summary Data - HUD Exchange per CPD Notice 24-04 Notice CPD-24-04: Low- and Moderate-Income Summary Data Updates - HUD Exchange . Due to the difference in coverage area and geometry, both the 2010 Tracts and 2020 Blocks that both show Low Moderate Income Percentage are used for FIPSA area 12057 and they are filtered to show 51% or greater LMI. Read more about the use of this data for ACA and HUD grants at: https://www.hud.gov/sites/dfiles/OA/documents/CPD-24-04.pdf Sharing and use: This data can be shared publicly. Created for: Hillsborough County Update Frequency: Annually Points of Contact: Equity & Community Impact, Assistant County Administrator - Cheryl Howell Web Map: ACA Equity and Community Impact - Overview
